message.content: {"answer": "B", "option_text": "A complex pulmonary arteriovenous malformation in the left lower lobe with multiple feeding arteries leading to pleural effusion and hemothorax.", "reason": "The chest X-ray (Figure 1) shows a large opacity in the left lower zone consistent with pleural effusion/hemothorax. The CT images (Figures 2 and 3) reveal a vascular mass in the left lower lobe with prominent feeding vessels, characteristic of a complex pulmonary arteriovenous malformation (PAVM). Rupture of a PAVM is a known cause of hemothorax. Options A, C, D, E, and F are inconsistent with the complex vascular morphology and hemorrhagic complication seen on CT."}
